title: Improved dsRNA Isolation and Purification Method in Saccharomyces cerevisiae
author: Cardoso, Elias, et al.
materials: Each 25 µl reaction included: reaction 1x Buffer 1, 2 or 3, 1 ng dsRNA, 30 U reverse transcriptase (NZY Reverse Transcriptase # MB12401, NZYTech, Portugal), 0.5 U Taq Pol (NZYTaq II DNA polymerase, # MB35402, NZYTech, Portugal), BSA (0.5 mg/ml, NEB #B9001S, USA), 0.1 mM dNTPs (Thermo, USA), 2.5 mM DTT (Sigma 646563), 10 µM each gene-specific primer (Table 1). Amplification conditions were: 39 °C for 90 min, then 5 min at 95 °C, followed by 45 cycles of 1 min at 94 °C, 1 min at 52 °C and 1 min at 72 °C, followed by a final extension step at 72 °C for 10 min carried out in a Sensoquest thermal cycler (Labcycle 48, Germany). The expected size was 650 bp.

steps.title: Prepare saturated phenol (pH 4 & 7)
steps.instruction: Make two batches of saturated phenol, one buffered to pH 4 and one to pH 7, following the sequence of melting, additive addition, washing, and storage.

substeps.instruction: Melt an aliquot of redistilled phenol in a 65 °C water bath or let it melt at room temperature overnight.
Add 8‑hydroxyquinoline to a final concentration of 0.1 % w/v; mix until dissolved (separate flasks for pH 4 and pH 7).
Add an equal volume of distilled sterile water, mix, and let the phases separate at room temperature for ~15–30 min.
Remove the aqueous (top) layer and discard it.
Repeat the water‑wash step three times using acetate buffer (pH 4) for the pH 4 batch or TE buffer (pH 7) for the pH 7 batch.
Add 0.1 % (v/v) 2‑mercaptoethanol to the aqueous phase, mix, and allow phases to separate.
Store the saturated phenol at 4 °C; it remains usable for up to 5 months.

steps.title: Break yeast cell walls
steps.instruction: Treat yeast pellets with an increased concentration of β‑mercaptoethanol to facilitate cell‑wall disruption.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the yeast pellet in the appropriate buffer (as used later for extraction).
Add β‑mercaptoethanol to a final concentration of 5 % (v/v) (increase from the original 2.5 %).
Incubate for 40 min (extended from the original 15 min) at ambient temperature with gentle mixing.

steps.title: Total nucleic‑acid extraction (first step)
steps.instruction: Extract total nucleic acids from the pre‑treated yeast cells; this extract can be used as input for downstream dsRNA isolation.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µl Extraction Buffer 1 to 50 mg of pre‑treated yeast cells, resuspend, then add 500 µl phenol (pH 7) and 100 µl chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (CIA).
Vortex 10 s and incubate at 60 °C for 30 min.
Centrifuge at 10 000 g for 10 min.
Transfer the ~500 µl supernatant to a new tube, add 100 µl CIA, vortex.
Centrifuge at 10 000 g for 10 min.
Transfer the supernatant to a fresh tube, add 1 volume 100 % isopropanol and 10 µl 2 M sodium acetate (pH 5.6).
Incubate at –20 °C for 30 min–1 h.
Centrifuge at 10 000 g, 4 °C for 10 min; discard supernatant.
Add 1 ml 70 % ethanol (pre‑chilled), centrifuge at 10 000 g, 4 °C for 1 min, discard supernatant.
Add 500 µl 100 % ethanol, leave 1 min, centrifuge at 10 000 g for 2 min, discard supernatant.
Air‑dry the pellet at room temperature until completely dry and resuspend in 50 µl STE buffer.

steps.title: dsRNA isolation – phenol phase‑partition (improved method)
steps.instruction: Extract dsRNA directly from yeast using the SS20 buffer, phenol/CIA extraction, ammonium acetate precipitation and ethanol washes.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µl Extraction Buffer 2 (SS20) to a nuclease‑free 1.5 ml tube containing 50 mg pre‑treated yeast pellet; vortex to resuspend.
Add 500 µl phenol (pH 4 or pH 7) and 50–100 µl CIA; vortex 10 s.
Incubate at 60 °C for 15–20 min, inverting the tube every 5–10 min; then cool to room temperature.
Centrifuge at 14 000 g for 10 min.
Transfer the aqueous upper phase to a new tube; add 450 µl phenol (same pH) and 45 µl CIA; vortex 5 s.
Incubate at room temperature for 15–20 min to form an emulsion.
Centrifuge at 12 000 g for 10 min at room temperature; transfer the aqueous phase to a new tube.
Add 100 µl CIA, vortex briefly, then centrifuge at 10 000 g for 10 min at room temperature.
Transfer the aqueous phase to a fresh tube and add 1 volume 7.5 M ammonium acetate; invert 5–6 times to mix.
Incubate at –20 °C for 30 min to precipitate dsRNA.
Centrifuge at 14 000 g for 15 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant.
Add 500 µl chilled (‑20 °C) 70 % ethanol, centrifuge at 10 000 g for 5 min, discard supernatant.
Add 500 µl 100 % ethanol, centrifuge at 10 000 g for 5 min, discard supernatant.
Air‑dry the pellet at room temperature until completely dry.
Resuspend the dsRNA pellet in 50 µl STE 1× buffer and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: dsRNA isolation – cellulose (reference method)
steps.instruction: Isolate dsRNA using fibrous cellulose as the binding matrix, followed by ethanol washes and precipitation.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µl Extraction Buffer 1 to 50 mg pre‑treated yeast cells, resuspend, then add 500 µl phenol (pH 7) and 100 µl CIA; vortex 10 s.
Incubate at 60 °C for 30 min, then centrifuge at 10 000 g for 10 min.
Transfer ~550 µl supernatant to a tube containing 75 mg fibrous cellulose.
Add 450 µl STE 1× buffer and 200 µl 100 % ethanol, vortex, incubate 5 min.
Centrifuge at 8 000 g for 3 min and discard supernatant.
Wash pellet with 1 ml STE + 16 % ethanol, centrifuge 8 000 g 3 min, discard supernatant. Repeat this wash (steps above) four times total.
Elute dsRNA: add 500 µl STE 1× (no ethanol), vortex, centrifuge 8 000 g 3 min, collect supernatant.
Add 250 µl STE 1×, vortex, centrifuge 8 000 g 3 min, collect supernatant and combine with the first eluate.
Precipitate dsRNA by adding 1 volume 100 % isopropanol and 10 µl 2 M sodium acetate (pH 5.6); incubate at –20 °C for 30 min–1 h.
Centrifuge at 10 000 g, 4 °C for 10 min; discard supernatant.
Wash pellet with 1 ml 70 % ethanol, centrifuge 10 000 g, 4 °C for 10 min, discard supernatant.
Air‑dry the pellet at room temperature and resuspend in 50 µl STE buffer.

steps.title: Denature dsRNA with DMSO (for RT‑PCR)
steps.instruction: Heat dsRNA in DMSO to disrupt secondary structure before reverse transcription.

substeps.instruction: Mix the purified dsRNA with DMSO to a final concentration of 10 % (v/v).
Heat the mixture at 95 °C for 1 min.
Immediately place on ice (or keep on ice) before adding to the RT‑PCR master mix.

steps.title: Prepare RT‑PCR master mix
steps.instruction: Assemble a 25 µl one‑tube RT‑PCR reaction containing all required enzymes, buffer, and primers.

substeps.instruction: Choose one of the three buffer systems:
• Buffer 1 (5× Green GoTaq® Flexi Buffer, Promega, pH 8.5, contains blue and yellow dyes).
• Buffer 2 (10× Taq Fermentas Buffer with KCl: 100 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.8 at 25 °C, 500 mM KCl, 0.8 % Nonidet P‑40).
• Buffer 3 (10× Taq Fermentas Buffer with (NH₄)₂SO₄: 750 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.8 at 25 °C, 200 mM (NH₄)₂SO₄, 0.1 % Tween 20).
In a PCR tube add:
– 1× of the selected buffer (adjust volume to give a final 1× concentration).
– 1 ng of denatured dsRNA.
– 30 U NZY Reverse Transcriptase (catalog # MB12401).
– 0.5 U NZYTaq II DNA polymerase (catalog # MB35402).
– BSA to a final concentration of 0.5 mg/ml (NEB # B9001S).
– 0.1 mM dNTP mix (Thermo).
– 2.5 mM DTT (Sigma # 646563).
– 10 µM each gene‑specific primer (L21/L22).
Bring the total volume to 25 µl with nuclease‑free water.

steps.title: Run RT‑PCR thermal program
steps.instruction: Cycling conditions for reverse transcription followed by PCR amplification.

substeps.instruction: 39 °C for 90 min (reverse transcription).
95 °C for 5 min (RT inactivation and initial denaturation).
45 cycles of:
– 94 °C for 1 min (denaturation),
– 52 °C for 1 min (annealing),
– 72 °C for 1 min (extension).
Final extension: 72 °C for 10 min.
Hold at 4 °C until samples are retrieved.
